cookies.label: Cookies
cookies.body: We use analytics cookies to see how the site is read. Declining breaks nothing — every part of it works the same either way, and you can change your mind whenever you like.

country.costIntro: The threshold is the investment alone. Transfer taxes, professional and government fees and the first renewal are not optional — everyone pays them, every time.
country.ctaBody: One partner works in each jurisdiction, and an enquiry reaches only them — and only if you tick the consent box. A person replies, usually within one working day.

notFound.heading: That page is not here
notFound.body: Either the address has a typo in it, or the page moved when a jurisdiction was rewritten. The comparison table is the fastest way back in — it lists every jurisdiction the site covers, with a link to each.

brief.heading: Tell us what you are looking for
brief.intro: Three answers are enough to start: a budget, a place, and what the property is for. It goes to the one partner who works in this jurisdiction, and they reply to you directly.
brief.cityHint: As specific as you can be. If you already know the answer changes with the district — as it does in Athens and in Lisbon — say which one.

brief.fine: We do not sell property and take no percentage of any transaction. Your brief goes to one partner, not to a list.

error.title: That did not go through.
error.body: An email address and the consent box are the two things we cannot proceed without. Everything else is optional.

broke.title: That is on us.
broke.body: The brief did not reach us — the fault is at our end, not in what you filled in. Write to {email} and we will pick it up from there.

alerts.heading: We write when a rule changes
alerts.body: Not a newsletter. A short email when a threshold, a tax or a requirement in one of these jurisdictions becomes something else — with the statute and the date. There will not be many: across 2026 there have been fewer than ten such changes across five countries. The confirmation brings the four routes compared on one printable sheet.
alerts.jurisdictionsHint: Optional. Leave them all unticked and you get all five.
alerts.consentLabel: Send me an email when a rule changes. I can unsubscribe by replying to any of them.
alerts.fine: We keep the address and nothing else, and pass it to nobody.

enquiry.stepsHeading: What happens after you press send

one.title: It reaches a mailbox, and a person reads it
one.body: It is not scored, it is not added to a mailing list, and it is not passed to anybody until you have said it may be. The consent box is that permission, and it covers one introduction rather than a list.

two.title: We work out which jurisdiction it actually fits
two.body: Against the same figures and the same statutes published on this site, each carrying the date it was last checked. Sometimes the answer is that none of the five fits what you are trying to do, and then that is what you are told.

three.title: We introduce you to one licensed firm
three.body: One firm, licensed in the country concerned, and you are told which and why that one. The firm pays us if it takes the introduction. You pay nothing, and nothing obliges you to instruct them.

calculator.metaTitle: What entry to a residency programme actually costs
calculator.metaDescription: Programmes name one figure and you pay more. The advertised minimum beside the real cost of entry in Greece, Portugal, Malta and the UAE — line by line, with the act that sets each one and the day it was read.
calculator.heading: What residency by investment actually costs
calculator.intro: Programmes advertise a minimum of {grLow} to {ptAdvertised}. You pay more: purchase taxes, contributions to the state, permit fees and intermediaries land on top. On Malta that extra is {mtGap}, a quarter of the whole sum. Name your own figure and see which of the four it covers.
calculator.verdictSome: A budget of {budget} covers entry to {n} of the four.
calculator.verdictAll: A budget of {budget} covers entry to all four. Dearest of them: {name} — {total}.
calculator.verdictNone: A budget of {budget} covers none of the four. Nearest: {name} — short by {short}.
calculator.emptyPrompt: Name a sum and the answer appears.
calculator.workingLabel: Show every cost, line by line
calculator.amountLabel: If the asset costs more than the minimum — its price
calculator.structureLabel: What the extra is made of

notes.gr: In Attica, Thessaloniki and the large islands the threshold is €800,000 — then it takes €866,000. For a listed restoration or a change of use it is €250,000 — then €274,000.
notes.pt: Property is excluded from the Portuguese programme by statute; the investment goes into a fund. Filing online takes 25% off the AIMA fees — about €3,400.
notes.mt: Housing can be leased rather than bought: €114,000 for the first year. But rent is spent, not staked, and it has to be evidenced every year for the first five.
notes.ae: The threshold is set in dirhams: AED 2,000,000. Converted at 4.288, read on 23 August 2026.

calculator.basisNote: One main applicant, no dependants: everything payable to enter and to hold the permit through its first renewal. Annual costs after that are on each jurisdiction's own page.
calculator.ctaHeading: Two routes fit. The next step is a firm licensed in the one you pick.
calculator.ctaNote: This site does not sell property and does not give legal advice. It finds you a licensed firm in the jurisdiction and tells you what it was told about you.
calculator.share: Copy a link to these numbers
calculator.updated: Lines read against their sources no later than {date}
calculator.method: Basis: one main applicant, no dependants, and everything payable to enter and to hold the permit through its first renewal. Family composition is not an input, because only two of the four jurisdictions publish a per-dependant figure and the Greek regulation sets none at all — a control that changed one country in four would misinform about three.

body.extrasHeading: The costs on top of the minimum investment
body.extrasLead: The extra above the advertised minimum comes from four sources. The programmes weight them differently, which is why the gap differs: from {ptShare} in Portugal to {mtShare} on Malta.
body.extrasTaxes: are charged on the price of the asset and grow with it. In Greece the transfer tax with its municipal surcharge is {grRate}, which on a {grAdvertised} property is {grTransferTax}. On Malta stamp duty is 5%, or {mtStampDuty}. In the UAE the land department's registration fee is 4%, or {aeDld}.
body.extrasState: exist only on Malta and come to {mtContribTotal}: an administrative fee of {mtAdminFee}, a government contribution of {mtContribution} and a compulsory donation to a registered NGO of {mtNgo}. They do not move with the price of the housing and are the same on the purchase and the lease route — which is why the Maltese gap is the largest.
body.extrasPermits: are usually the smallest and the most predictable. In Portugal they are not: {ptAnalysis} to consider the application, {ptGrant} to grant it, {ptRenewal} for the first renewal. Filing online takes 25% off them.
body.extrasAgents: are the one group you can negotiate over, and the one where we have no statute — only market practice. Those lines are marked as such in the working.
body.countriesHeading: The cost of residency by investment, country by country
body.grText: The threshold depends on where the property is and what it is. {grAdvertised} covers the whole country except Attica, Thessaloniki and the large islands; there it is {grHigh}, and entry costs {grHighReal}. The {grLow} threshold is open only for a listed restoration or a change of use, where entry costs {grLowReal}. Of the {grGap} extra, nearly half is the lawyer and the agent.
body.aeHeading: UAE golden visa — {aeAed} advertised, {aeReal} in reality
body.aeText: The minimum is set in dirhams, so its price in euro moves with the rate; on {aeDate} it was {aeAdvertised}. It need not be a single property — several qualify on their combined value. More than half of the {aeGap} extra is the land department's registration fee.
body.mtText: The largest gap of the four: {mtGap} on top, a quarter of the whole sum. The cause is the contributions to the state, which do not move with the price of the housing. Housing can be leased rather than bought, from {mtRent} a year: the first year then costs {mtRentFirstYear}, but rent is spent rather than staked, and it has to be evidenced every year for the first five.
body.ptHeading: Portugal golden visa — {ptAdvertised} advertised, {ptReal} in reality
body.ptText: The smallest gap, {ptShare}. Property has been excluded from this programme by statute since 2023; the investment goes into a fund. Most of the extra is the AIMA fees and the fund's charges for the first year. Filing online takes 25% off the fees, about {ptOnlineSaving}.
body.excludedHeading: What the figure excludes: family, later renewals, ownership
body.excludedLead: The calculation is for one main applicant with no dependants, carried to the first renewal of the permit. Four things sit outside it.
body.excludedFamily: A checkable per-dependant figure is published in only two of the four jurisdictions, and the Greek regulation sets none at all. We do not publish a field that would be right about two countries and invented about two others.
body.excludedAfter: the second renewal and those after it, the fund's charges from the second year, the Maltese lease from the second year.
body.excludedRate: The Emirati threshold is set in dirhams, so its price in euro moves with the exchange rate.
body.sourcesHeading: Where the figures come from and how to check them
body.sourcesText: Under every line in the working stands the act that sets it and the day that act was read. Lines carry one of three levels: statute, secondary source, market practice. The third — the lawyer and the agent — is the only one where the sum is negotiable; everything else moves only when the law does.

gr.transfer-tax: Charged on the taxable value, which is not always the price paid.
gr.notary: The first band of the tariff is disputed: 0.80% in the codified text, 1% in two legal publishers. The lower figure is used.

mt.stamp-duty: No reduced rate is open to a buyer who would have needed ministerial permission.
mt.rent: Rent is a cost, not a stake. Nothing is committed on this route.

ae.dld-transfer: The instrument splits this fee equally with the seller «unless agreed otherwise». Budget it, but it is negotiable.
ae.agency: VAT at 5% applies to the commission and is not included here.
